newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower on weekend profit taking.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower on weekend profit taking.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed lower ahead of the weekend as insitutional investors continued to sit on the sidelines, dealers and analysts said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended 4.54 points lower to 1,232.38, while the small-cap Second Board index was down 1.31 to 607.01.
"Volumes picked up a little and the selling was absorbed quite well. There was definitely the 'Friday effect' at play," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
At the close, 256 million shares changed hands.
The value of shares traded was 1,713 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers by 306 to 280.
"There was some institutional buying of blue-chip stocks but it was very selective. The (Composite) Index was down, but in a very narrow range," said a dealer at a local equities brokerage house.
Blue chip stocks were still on an uptrend, he said. But speculative, smaller-capitalised issues were attracting most of the interest.
Infrastructure developer Intria was down 10 cents to 6.00 ringgit after a local research house downgraded the stock.
